AMD and Intel plan shared oneDNN optimization path for PyTorch on CPUs

AMD says it and Intel have aligned on oneDNN, an open-source acceleration library, for PyTorch, an AI software framework. The collaboration announced October 20 would integrate optimizations from ZenDNN, AMD’s CPU inference library, into oneDNN. AMD’s announcement says the companies have aligned on oneDNN as the default open-source library for accelerating PyTorch on x86, the processor architecture used by their CPUs. AMD will contribute optimizations from ZenDNN, its library for inference—the execution of trained AI models—while continuing to tune software for its own processors. Data Phoenix reports the planned integration and the companies’ goal of simplifying application development, maintenance and deployment. The intended change is a common destination for optimization work that has been maintained separately, giving developers deploying across both vendors a shared library path. The agreement follows a recommendation from the x86 Ecosystem Advisory Group, according to AMD. CloudNews.Tech describes it as a group AMD and Intel created in 2024. AMD’s ZenDNN repository describes a library intended for use through supported frameworks rather than independently. Its documentation describes separate integration plugins for PyTorch and TensorFlow, another AI framework. Hardware Busters describes the move from separately maintained ZenDNN optimizations into oneDNN. It also reports that AMD previously participated in the library’s governing foundation as a general contributor. AMD says it has now joined the Unified Acceleration Foundation, or UXL, as a steering member, giving it a place on the body governing oneDNN. For teams maintaining PyTorch applications across AMD and Intel CPUs, Data Phoenix identifies the intended benefit as avoiding separate vendor optimization paths. Simpler development, maintenance and deployment are the collaboration’s stated goals. For existing ZenDNN users, AMD’s repository still directs PyTorch users to zentorch, its integration plugin, for compatibility and installation details. That remains the documented route.
